findings.description: REQUEST section uses letter-based step labels (Step A, Step B, Step C, Step D) instead of integer step numbers (1, 2, 3, 4). Standard 4 requires integer-only step numbering in SOP documents. These four steps are procedural steps the user must execute in sequence, not mnemonic phase-type identifiers.

scope_notes: docs/dev/ is excluded from the style-inspector's primary audit scope per spec. Findings here are advisory unless the orchestrator explicitly includes the file.

The bash code blocks in this file are user-pasteable SOP commands, not production scripts. Standards 2 (no-hardcoded-values), 3 (use-source-venv), 9 (parameterized-scripts), and 10 (dangling-references) were not applied to the inline bash code per orchestrator instruction.
Sub-step labels D1/D2/T1/T2/C1/V1 are mnemonic phase-type identifiers (Discover / Transform / Commit / Verify), not step numbers. They are not violations of Standard 4.
Source 3a / Source 3b labels appear only inside Python string literals destined for target-file bash comments. They are content data, not SOP step labels, and are not violations.
No marketing language or story-style narrative found (Standard 8 passes for the prose sections).
No decimal step numbering (e.g., 1.1, 1.2) found in the integer step sequences.
summary: One advisory finding: the REQUEST section uses letter-based step labels (Step A–D) rather than integer step numbers (1–4), violating Standard 4. All other applicable documentation standards pass: no Chinese text, no marketing language, no decimal step numbering in the main ordered sequences, no filename convention violations. The file is in docs/dev/ (excluded from primary audit scope), so all findings are advisory.
